comparison.objective: Commission a locked shock-absorber setting through repeated physical cycles, versus accurately pin a notice to a marked position on a tilted corkboard.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate requires hex-key seating, fastener unlocking/relocking, fine rotary adjustment, counterholding, and guarded cycle inspection. PR-1991 requires holding a sliding card aligned while orienting and forcefully inserting a small pushpin through it into cork.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires two ≥0.85 J stops within the 12 mm stroke without hard-stop strike, overload, excessive rebound, or lock drift. PR-1991 requires a seated pin through the notice, top-edge and angular alignment, both grippers clear, and two seconds of stable support.
comparison.reason: Small-tool alignment, bimanual holding, and force application are shared generic primitives. Pushpin insertion that permanently supports an aligned card tests a different outcome and manipulation mechanism from unlocking, tuning, relocking, and dynamically validating a damper. Candidate drift and response limits are partly undeclared.
